content.text: The container doesn’t expose block device nodes, so I’ll try from the host context where mounting should actually work.

arguments.command:
set -e
lsblk -o NAME,PATH,SIZE,FSTYPE,LABEL,UUID,MOUNTPOINTS,TRAN,MODEL,RM,RO
mkdir -p /mnt/usb
# Pick an unmounted removable/USB partition if present, otherwise an unmounted USB/removable disk with a filesystem.
dev="$(lsblk -rpno PATH,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,TRAN,RM,RO | awk '$2=="part" && $3!="" && $4=="" && ($5=="usb" || $6=="1") && $7=="0" {print $1; exit}')"
if [ -z "$dev" ]; then
  dev="$(lsblk -rpno PATH,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,TRAN,RM,RO | awk '$2=="disk" && $3!="" && $4=="" && ($5=="usb" || $6=="1") {print $1; exit}')"
fi
if [ -z "$dev" ]; then
  # read-only removable/usb fallback, mount read-only
  dev="$(lsblk -rpno PATH,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,TRAN,RM,RO | awk '$3!="" && $4=="" && ($5=="usb" || $6=="1") {print $1; exit}')"
fi
if [ -z "$dev" ]; then
  echo "No unmounted USB/removable block device with a detectable filesystem found." >&2
  exit 2
fi
ro="$(lsblk -rno RO "$dev" | head -1)"
if [ "$ro" = "1" ]; then
  mount -o ro "$dev" /mnt/usb
else
  mount "$dev" /mnt/usb
fi
echo "Mounted $dev at /mnt/usb"
findmnt /mnt/usb

I can see a likely attached drive:


…but this OpenClaw container does **not** expose `/dev/vdb` as an actual device node, and host-level elevated commands are disabled for this webchat session. So I can’t mount it myself from here.

To mount it on the host, run:

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/usb
sudo mount -o ro /dev/vdb /mnt/usb
findmnt /mnt/usb
```

I used `-o ro` because `lsblk` reports `/dev/vdb` as read-only. If it has a partition instead of a filesystem directly on the disk, use the partition path shown by `lsblk`, e.g. `/dev/vdb1`, instead of `/dev/vdb`.
